svg.title: Past search schematic 04: how deep: the scroll's “dig N cubits” against the depths searches reached
svg.text: Past searches 04 — how deep: the scroll's “dig N cubits” against the depths searches reached
Depth axis to scale. Red = the scroll's stated depths. Blue = depths that the sources give for searches in the ledger.
Red dot at 0.5 m per cubit; whisker 0.445–0.525 m (short to royal cubit). Stems run from the surface.
Blue bar = dug or cleared to that depth. Diamond = depth of a find. Dashed = depth not given as a figure.
The scroll: “dig N cubits”, with entries

“hardly more than eighteen inches”; the rock's magnetism masked metal
the cave's documents had lain 0.30–0.40 m deep

a deposit “several metres deep”; no figure given
cleared ≈ 6.1 m (20 ft), not bottomed; perhaps “a further fifty
feet” (≈ 15 m) below, by Allegro's guess
named-place dig, not a scroll search; Bull 1968
bedrock ≈ 7.6 m (25 ft) beside Building B;
white tick: ≈ 5.2 m (17 ft) of fill inside the N wall
The red rows list every “dig N cubits” in the project
translation. They are read as depth below the surface, as
most editors read them; the text does not say where the

16 of 26 entries say seven cubits (≈ 3.5 m) or more.
The deepest scroll-motivated digging with a figure:
the Cave 13 pits at about 2.5 m (stopped as unsafe)
and the Cypros shaft at about 6 m (not bottomed).
Cave 3's documents lay only 0.30–0.40 m deep.
Christmas Cave (S05): stopped at the Roman floor.
Gutfeld's tunnel at Kh. Mird, 2000–04: a dead end.
“Dig three [cu]bits” (≈ 1.5 m) at the cave of the pillar.
Ledger rows tied to it: S09 Twin Cave (a deposit several
metres deep), S10 in 1986 (depth not given), S14 Jones's
pit (to bedrock) and S20 cave IV/11 (coins in an upper
Project translation (text/translation_en.json) and entry lines (atlas/app/atlas-data.json); search
ledger, research/history/salvage_records/searches.csv; Allegro, Treasure of the Copper Scroll, 2nd
ed. (1964) pp. 67, 75; Patrich and Arubas 1989; Bull 1968 pp. 66, 68; ESI 6 pp. 68–70.
Depth axis to scale, 0–13 m; the Cypros arrow runs off it. The build checks each “dig” phrase against
the translation and stops if an entry with “dig” is missing from the chart.
Most of the scroll's stated depths are metres, not centimetres. The searches that give a figure
stopped short of most of them, or used detectors that saw about half a metre.
Where any deposit is. The depths have no known datum and ground levels have changed since antiquity,
so a dig to the stated depth at the wrong spot tests nothing.
